_shape: Each tool: name, by, what (one sentence), docs (URL), std (standard keys from progress.json, optional), phase (phase id from progress.json, optional).

categories.name: Start here
categories.blurb: Read these before writing the Awaken loop. They explain the patterns everything else is built on.

tools.name: Building effective agents
tools.what: When to use a simple workflow and when to use an agent, plus the core patterns: prompt chaining, routing, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer.

tools.name: ReAct paper
tools.what: The reason → act → observe loop that most agents, including Awaken, are based on.

tools.name: Hugging Face Agents Course
tools.what: A free course that builds agents step by step with smolagents, LangGraph and LlamaIndex.

tools.name: Claude Cookbooks
tools.what: Runnable notebooks for tool use, RAG, sub-agents and evaluation.

categories.name: Models & SDKs
categories.blurb: The LLM that acts as the agent's central nervous system, and the SDKs for calling it.

tools.name: Claude API
tools.what: Messages API, streaming, prompt caching and model reference.

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK
tools.what: A production agent loop with built-in tools, permissions and sub-agents. Useful to compare against our hand-built loop.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.what: Run open models locally on the M1 for free, offline experiments.

tools.name: Transformers
tools.what: Load and run open models in PyTorch. Connects Phase 1 to the LLM layer.

categories.name: Function calling
categories.blurb: How the model asks to run a tool with arguments that match a schema.

tools.name: Tool use with Claude
tools.what: Define tools with JSON Schema, handle tool_use blocks and return tool results.

tools.name: Function calling guide
tools.what: The same idea in the OpenAI API, including strict schema mode.

tools.name: JSON Schema
tools.what: The schema language both APIs use to describe tool arguments.

categories.name: Protocols
categories.blurb: Open standards for connecting agents to tools and data, and to each other.

tools.name: Model Context Protocol
tools.what: The spec and guides for MCP servers (which expose tools and data) and clients (which use them).

tools.name: MCP SDKs & servers
tools.what: Official Python and TypeScript SDKs plus reference servers to learn from.

tools.name: Agent Communication Protocol
tools.what: A REST-based protocol for agents to discover each other and exchange messages and tasks.

tools.name: A2A Protocol
tools.what: Agent-to-agent protocol for passing tasks between agents built on different frameworks.

tools.name: AGNTCY
tools.what: Infrastructure for agent networks, home of the Agent Gateway Protocol (AGP).

categories.name: Multi-agent frameworks
categories.blurb: For Phase 4: rebuild our Planner / Researcher / Executor / Reviewer flow in one of these and compare.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.what: Agents as graphs of nodes with shared state, checkpoints and human-in-the-loop interrupts.

tools.name: LangGraph interrupts
tools.what: Pause a graph and wait for a human to approve or edit before continuing.

tools.name: AutoGen
tools.what: Multi-agent conversations where agents with different roles talk until a task is done.

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.what: Role-based crews of agents with tasks and processes.

tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.what: Lightweight agents with handoffs between agents, guardrails and tracing.

categories.name: Memory & retrieval
categories.blurb: Short-term scratchpads and long-term memory in vector databases, plus RAG.

tools.name: LangGraph memory
tools.what: Short-term (thread) and long-term (store) memory patterns for agents.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.what: An open-source vector database that runs locally. An easy first long-term memory.

tools.name: FAISS
tools.what: A fast similarity-search library. Good for understanding how vector search works.

tools.name: pgvector
tools.what: Vector search inside Postgres, for when memory needs a real database.

tools.name: LlamaIndex
tools.what: Load, index and query documents for retrieval-augmented generation.

categories.name: Sandboxing & security
categories.blurb: Keep agents isolated, give them only the access they need, and verify who they are.

tools.name: E2B
tools.what: Cloud sandboxes for running agent-generated code safely.

tools.name: Docker
tools.what: Run code tools in containers so they can't touch the host.

tools.name: OAuth 2.0
tools.what: The spec family behind machine-to-machine tokens, including the client-credentials flow.

tools.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps
tools.what: The main risks for LLM apps and agents, including prompt injection and excessive agency.

categories.name: Evaluation & observability
categories.blurb: See what an agent did at each step and measure whether it worked.

tools.name: Inspect
tools.what: An open-source framework for writing evaluations of models and agents.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.what: Open-source tracing, prompt management and evals. Can be self-hosted.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.what: Tracing and evaluation for LangChain and LangGraph apps.

tools.name: PyTorch
tools.what: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module and the mps backend for the M1.

tools.name: NumPy
tools.what: The array library Genesis is built on.

_repos_shape: Each repo: repo (owner/name on GitHub), kind (Platform, Framework, Coding agent, Protocol, Memory, Browser), what (one sentence), stars (snapshot used when the live GitHub count can't load), std/phase optional like tools.

repos.what: Workflow automation with AI agent nodes: wire LLMs to 400+ apps visually or in code.
The project that started the autonomous-agent wave in 2023, now a platform for building and running agents.
Build agentic workflows and RAG pipelines in a visual editor, then ship them as apps or APIs.
Drag-and-drop builder for agents and workflows, with every flow exportable as an API.
Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal: reads the codebase, edits files, runs commands.
The most-used library for chaining LLM calls, tools and retrieval into agents.
OpenAI's lightweight coding agent for the terminal, written in Rust.
Lets an agent drive a real web browser: click, type and read pages to finish tasks.
Google's open-source agent that brings Gemini into the terminal, with MCP support.
Reference MCP servers (filesystem, Git, fetch, memory) that any MCP client can plug in.
Open platform for software-engineering agents that write code, run it and browse docs in a sandbox.
Multi-agent framework that gives agents roles like PM, architect and engineer to build software together.
Lets an LLM run code on your own computer to get things done, with approval before each step.
A memory layer that lets agents remember users and facts across sessions.
Microsoft's framework for agents that talk to each other to solve tasks.
Orchestrates role-playing agents as a crew with tasks, delegation and shared goals.
Build AI agents visually with drag-and-drop nodes on top of LangChain.
Connects agents to your documents: parsing, indexing and retrieval (RAG).
Builds agents as graphs with persistent state, checkpoints and human-in-the-loop pauses.
Fast framework for building, running and managing agents and agent teams.
OpenAI's lightweight SDK for agents, handoffs, guardrails and tracing.
A barebones library for agents that write their actions as Python code.
